title: Tandem cadence brief — 1:1 prep for Kai
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable 1:1 with Elyse (report) — align priorities for next sprint, unblock career conversation, and decide on canary rollout ownership.

Context (short):
- Elyse ramped up on runtime optimizations (KV cache) last quarter; took lead on perf benchmarks for v1.2.
- Team planning to start canary rollout of quantized model variant next week. Need clear owner for incident response and rollback threshold.
- Elyse mentioned interest in IC laddering and taking on a small tech lead scope.

Goals for this 25-minute sync:
1) Confirm Elyse's preferred ownership model for canary (on-call rotation vs single owner).
2) Surface any hidden blockers (infra creds, model artifacts, infra quotas).
3) Career check-in: understand what success looks like for Elyse in next 6 months and concrete next steps.
4) Capture 2–3 action items we can close before next 1:1.

Agenda (timed):
- 0:00–2:00 quick personal check-in (how are you, energy, interruptions).
- 2:00–9:00 async status on canary prep + checklist review (who has tested rollback, perf thresholds, dashboards).
- 9:00–16:00 blockers and resource asks (infra, QA time, partner review).
- 16:00–22:00 career conversation: interests, stretch areas, mentorship plan.
- 22:00–25:00 recap + concrete action items & owners.

Prep notes for me (manager):
- Bring perf dashboard link and current RPS/latency numbers (quick numbers to mention:  p50 85ms, p99 230ms on staging with 8k tokens).
- Have canary runbook open: canary success metric = <1% upstream error delta + no p99 regression > 10% vs baseline. Propose rollback threshold at 1.5x p99 delta.
- Be ready to propose a 2-week mentorship loop: pair on a postmortem + lead a small cross-team sync.
- Ask about time allocation: is Elyse comfortable dedicating 25% of next sprint to oncalling the canary? If not, what needs to change?

Open questions to surface to Elyse:
- Do you want rotational ownership for canary (spread ops burden) or single-owner for continuity? Pros/cons from your POV?
- Any lingering infra permissions or GCP quota issues blocking smoke tests?
- Are there any signals we should add to the dashboard (memory spikes, kv cache hit rate by user group)?
- For career stretch: technical leadership, cross-team collaboration, or architecture design — which would you prefer as next focus?

Risk/concerns (my notes):
- Team currently thin on SRE overlap next Tuesday (holiday); if canary starts then we need an explicit backup.
- QA stamp is still pending for quantized artifact — ETA Thu. If delayed, need a contingency plan.

Draft proposals to discuss (pick 1):
A) Rotational ownership: 2-week rotation among 3 engineers, Elyse as lead for first rotation + handoff doc.
B) Single owner: Elyse owns canary for first 4 weeks with weekly async check-ins with SRE. Manager backs time for mentoring and postmortem facilitation.

Desired outcome by end of meeting (explicit):
- Ownership model decided and documented in the runbook.
- 3 action items created (owner + due date).
- Elyse has one concrete career step to work on (e.g., lead the retro + write a short RFC).

Action items (template to assign in meeting):
- Owner: Elyse — finish canary smoke test and attach results to JIRA-ENG-1137. Due: 2026-11-18.
- Owner: Kai (me) — reserve SRE backup for first three canary days and confirm with Ravi. Due: 2026-11-15.
- Owner: Elyse + Kai — write 1-page handoff + incident runbook snippet (location: confluence/eng/canary-v1.2). Due: 2026-11-19.

Notes to self (post-meeting):
- If Elyse prefers rotational model, put her as first rotation lead to give continuity.
- Keep career conversation factual: list recent wins (benchmarks, PR sizes, cross-team syncs) and ask for one measurable goal.
- Follow up with a 30-min mentorship kickoff if Elyse asks for mentoring time.

Quick check list to confirm in the meeting:
- [ ] Dashboard links present and shared in Slack #runtime-canary.
- [ ] QA sign-off status confirmed.
- [ ] SRE backup confirmed for first 72 hours.
- [ ] Runbook updated with rollback threshold and owner field.

End of doc — quick ad-hoc thoughts:
- Consider creating a short template for future 1:1s to accelerate career conversations (3 bullets: wins, gaps, ask). Might convert into a tiny Google Doc template.
